newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turkish Cypriot leader calls for dialogue.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Cypriot leader calls for dialogue.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on Monday called for dialogue after his forces shot dead a 58-year-old Greek Cypriot who had crossed to the Turkish side of the divided island.

"For both Turks and Greeks, this death is a bitter event. The way to remove the reasons that caused these events lies with the negotiating table," the Turkish Cypriot news agency TAK quoted Denktash as saying.
Turkish authorities said the Greek Cypriot man, Petros Kakouli, on Sunday crossed 200 metres (yards) into the self-proclaimed Turkish Cypriot state and ignored orders to halt.
However, the man's son-in-law, who said he witnessed the shooting, said Turkish forces shot and killed Kakouli after he had tried to surrender.
Cyprus lodged protests with members of the U.N. Security Council on Monday over the incident.
The killing of Kakouli raised to five -- four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot -- the number of people killed along the buffer zone, which divides the island, since June.
In the Turkish capital Ankara foreign ministry spokesman Omer Akbel accused the Greek Cypriot side of having "opted for a policy of tension rather than negotiations on the island".

The island has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 after a Greek-engineered coup on the island. A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north, recognised only by Ankara, was established in 1983.
